definition.en: Highly skilled or proficient at something
definition.es: Hábil o experto en algo

examples.sentence: She is adept at reading subtle cues.
examples.translation: Es experta en leer señales sutiles.

vocabulary.notes: Usually followed by at + noun or -ing form.

definition.en: Apparently, although the real situation may be different
definition.es: Aparentemente, aunque la realidad puede ser distinta

examples.sentence: The ostensibly generous offer concealed several conditions.
examples.translation: La oferta aparentemente generosa ocultaba varias condiciones.

vocabulary.notes: Often signals a contrast between appearance and reality.

definition.en: To make a problem or unpleasant situation worse
definition.es: Empeorar o agravar un problema

examples.sentence: A careless comment could exacerbate the tension.
examples.translation: Un comentario descuidado podría agravar la tensión.

vocabulary.notes: Do not confuse with exasperate, which means to irritate someone.

definition.en: To make two opposing ideas or situations compatible
definition.es: Conciliar o hacer compatibles dos cosas opuestas

examples.sentence: The team had to reconcile speed with accuracy.
examples.translation: El equipo tuvo que conciliar la velocidad con la precisión.

vocabulary.notes: Reconcile A with B; a person can also be reconciled to a difficult fact.

definition.en: Treating a serious subject with inappropriate humor
definition.es: Burlón o poco serio ante un tema serio

examples.sentence: His facetious remark landed badly in the tense meeting.
examples.translation: Su comentario burlón cayó mal en la reunión tensa.

vocabulary.notes: It usually has a negative sense: the humor is not appropriate.

definition.en: Convenient and practical, especially for a short-term purpose
definition.es: Conveniente y práctico, sobre todo a corto plazo

examples.sentence: The expedient solution created a larger cost later.
examples.translation: La solución práctica creó un coste mayor después.

vocabulary.notes: Can imply that practicality has been chosen over principle.

definition.en: To cause an event or situation to happen suddenly
definition.es: Provocar que algo ocurra de repente

examples.sentence: The leaked report precipitated a leadership crisis.
examples.translation: El informe filtrado provocó una crisis de liderazgo.

vocabulary.notes: As an adjective, precipitate means rash or done too quickly.

definition.en: To accept something reluctantly without protesting
definition.es: Consentir o aceptar pasivamente, a menudo con desgana

examples.sentence: She refused to acquiesce to the investor's demands.
examples.translation: Se negó a consentir las exigencias del inversor.

vocabulary.notes: The preposition is normally to, not with.

definition.en: In agreement or harmony with something
definition.es: Acorde o compatible con algo

examples.sentence: Her decision was consonant with the company's values.
examples.translation: Su decisión era acorde con los valores de la empresa.

vocabulary.notes: In this meaning, use consonant with, not consonant to.

definition.en: A person or group affected by or interested in an organization
definition.es: Persona o grupo afectado por una organización o interesado en ella

examples.sentence: Every stakeholder deserved a voice in the decision.
examples.translation: Cada parte interesada merecía voz en la decisión.

vocabulary.notes: Broader than shareholder: it includes employees, communities and customers.

definition.en: Able to work successfully or be carried out effectively
definition.es: Viable; capaz de funcionar o llevarse a cabo

examples.sentence: The team needed a viable plan before scaling up.
examples.translation: El equipo necesitaba un plan viable antes de crecer.

vocabulary.notes: Viable describes a possibility; it does not necessarily mean ideal.

definition.en: To use an advantage or resource to achieve a desired result
definition.es: Aprovechar una ventaja o recurso para lograr un resultado

examples.sentence: The small studio leveraged its community to find early customers.
examples.translation: El pequeño estudio aprovechó su comunidad para encontrar clientes iniciales.

vocabulary.notes: Common in business English; as a noun, leverage can also mean borrowed financial power.

definition.en: Showing subtle differences, meanings or distinctions
definition.es: Que muestra diferencias o matices sutiles

examples.sentence: The model offered a more nuanced view of human intent.
examples.translation: El modelo ofrecía una visión más matizada de la intención humana.

vocabulary.notes: Often used approvingly for careful analysis.

definition.en: Present or felt throughout a place, thing or situation
definition.es: Extendido y presente por todas partes

examples.sentence: A pervasive fear of surveillance shaped the design.
examples.translation: Un miedo extendido a la vigilancia condicionó el diseño.

vocabulary.notes: Stronger than common: it suggests something is difficult to escape.

definition.en: To correct an unfair situation or remedy a problem
definition.es: Reparar una injusticia o corregir un problema

examples.sentence: The committee was created to redress the imbalance.
examples.translation: El comité se creó para corregir el desequilibrio.

vocabulary.notes: As a noun, redress can mean a remedy or compensation.

definition.en: Most noticeable or important
definition.es: Más destacado o importante

examples.sentence: The salient question was who would bear the risk.
examples.translation: La pregunta más importante era quién asumiría el riesgo.

vocabulary.notes: Useful when narrowing a complex discussion to its central point.

definition.en: An existing system, tradition or situation inherited from the past
definition.es: Sistema, tradición o situación heredada del pasado

examples.sentence: The company spent years untangling its legacy systems.
examples.translation: La empresa pasó años desenredando sus sistemas heredados.

vocabulary.notes: In technology, legacy often describes old software that is still essential.

definition.en: Developed through repeated cycles of testing and improvement
definition.es: Desarrollado mediante ciclos repetidos de prueba y mejora

examples.sentence: An iterative process allowed the team to learn from each failure.
examples.translation: Un proceso iterativo permitió al equipo aprender de cada fallo.

vocabulary.notes: Common in product, design and research contexts.

definition.en: To treat something as less urgent or important
definition.es: Considerar algo menos urgente o importante

examples.sentence: They deprioritized speed in favor of reliability.
examples.translation: Dieron menos prioridad a la velocidad en favor de la fiabilidad.

vocabulary.notes: A useful modern verb in planning and product conversations.

definition.en: Able to grow or be adapted without losing effectiveness
definition.es: Capaz de crecer sin perder eficacia

examples.sentence: The prototype was elegant but not yet scalable.
examples.translation: El prototipo era elegante, pero aún no escalable.

vocabulary.notes: Frequently used for systems, businesses and processes.

definition.en: A proposed explanation that can be tested
definition.es: Explicación propuesta que puede comprobarse

examples.sentence: The results did not support the original hypothesis.
examples.translation: Los resultados no respaldaron la hipótesis original.

vocabulary.notes: The plural is hypotheses, pronounced with a z sound at the end.

definition.en: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory alone
definition.es: Basado en la observación o el experimento

examples.sentence: The claim needed empirical support before publication.
examples.translation: La afirmación necesitaba respaldo empírico antes de publicarse.

vocabulary.notes: It contrasts with purely theoretical reasoning.

definition.en: To repeat a study or process and obtain comparable results
definition.es: Repetir un estudio o proceso y obtener resultados comparables

examples.sentence: A second lab could not replicate the celebrated finding.
examples.translation: Un segundo laboratorio no pudo replicar el hallazgo celebrado.

vocabulary.notes: In research, replication strengthens confidence in a result.

definition.en: To examine something very carefully and critically
definition.es: Examinar algo con mucha atención y de forma crítica

examples.sentence: Reviewers scrutinized every assumption in the methodology.
examples.translation: Los revisores examinaron cada supuesto de la metodología.

vocabulary.notes: Usually implies careful attention to possible flaws.

definition.en: A system of methods used in a particular area of study
definition.es: Sistema de métodos usado en un área de estudio

examples.sentence: The paper explained its methodology with unusual clarity.
examples.translation: El artículo explicó su metodología con una claridad poco habitual.

vocabulary.notes: Methodology is the study or rationale of methods, not just a single method.

definition.en: Not certain or definite because more evidence is needed
definition.es: Provisional o no definitivo porque hace falta más evidencia

examples.sentence: The tentative conclusion invited further questions.
examples.translation: La conclusión provisional invitaba a más preguntas.

vocabulary.notes: It can also describe a hesitant action or person.

definition.en: To confirm or support a statement with additional evidence
definition.es: Confirmar o respaldar algo con evidencia adicional

examples.sentence: The field notes corroborated the villagers' account.
examples.translation: Las notas de campo corroboraron el relato de los habitantes.

vocabulary.notes: Often used with testimony, evidence, accounts or findings.

definition.en: An opinion or conclusion based on incomplete information
definition.es: Opinión o conclusión basada en información incompleta

examples.sentence: Without a control group, the explanation remained conjecture.
examples.translation: Sin grupo de control, la explicación seguía siendo una conjetura.

vocabulary.notes: It can also be used as a verb: to conjecture that something is true.

definition.en: Belonging naturally to a particular place or region
definition.es: Originario de un lugar o región determinados

examples.sentence: The guide introduced us to an indigenous weaving tradition.
examples.translation: La guía nos presentó una tradición de tejido indígena.

vocabulary.notes: Use respectfully and specify a community when possible.

definition.en: To travel across or through a difficult area
definition.es: Atravesar o recorrer una zona, a menudo difícil

examples.sentence: We traversed the valley before the heat became unbearable.
examples.translation: Atravesamos el valle antes de que el calor fuera insoportable.

vocabulary.notes: More formal and vivid than simply walk across.

definition.en: Usual or traditional in a particular place or situation
definition.es: Habitual o tradicional en un lugar o situación

examples.sentence: It is customary to leave bread for the returning fishermen.
examples.translation: Es costumbre dejar pan para los pescadores que regresan.

vocabulary.notes: Customary refers to a social habit rather than a legal requirement.

definition.en: Relating to a transitional stage between two conditions
definition.es: Relacionado con una etapa de transición entre dos estados

examples.sentence: The station felt liminal, neither destination nor departure.
examples.translation: La estación se sentía liminal, ni destino ni partida.

vocabulary.notes: A literary term for a threshold or in-between state.

definition.en: A population dispersed from its original homeland
definition.es: Población dispersa fuera de su tierra de origen

examples.sentence: The festival is sustained by a far-reaching diaspora.
examples.translation: El festival se mantiene gracias a una diáspora extendida.

vocabulary.notes: Often refers to a community that maintains cultural ties across countries.

definition.en: The practice of exchanging things of equivalent value
definition.es: Intercambio mutuo de cosas de valor equivalente

examples.sentence: The arrangement depended on reciprocity rather than payment.
examples.translation: El acuerdo dependía de la reciprocidad y no del pago.

vocabulary.notes: It can describe social, diplomatic or economic relationships.

definition.en: The capacity to recover and adapt after difficulty
definition.es: Capacidad de recuperarse y adaptarse tras una dificultad

examples.sentence: Resilience is not the absence of grief but the ability to move with it.
examples.translation: La resiliencia no es ausencia de dolor, sino capacidad de avanzar con él.

vocabulary.notes: Often used for people, communities, materials and ecosystems.

definition.en: A person or event that causes a change or action
definition.es: Persona o acontecimiento que provoca un cambio o una acción

examples.sentence: The difficult conversation became a catalyst for change.
examples.translation: La conversación difícil se convirtió en un catalizador del cambio.

vocabulary.notes: A catalyst accelerates change without necessarily causing it alone.

definition.en: The examination of one's own thoughts and feelings
definition.es: Examen de los propios pensamientos y sentimientos

examples.sentence: A little introspection revealed why the goal felt borrowed.
examples.translation: Un poco de introspección reveló por qué el objetivo parecía ajeno.

vocabulary.notes: It is more inward-looking than general reflection.

definition.en: Done consciously and carefully rather than impulsively
definition.es: Hecho de manera consciente y cuidadosa, no impulsiva

examples.sentence: She took a deliberate pause before answering.
examples.translation: Hizo una pausa deliberada antes de responder.

vocabulary.notes: As a verb, deliberate means to think or discuss carefully.

definition.en: Calmness and emotional balance in a difficult situation
definition.es: Serenidad y equilibrio emocional en una situación difícil

examples.sentence: He handled the criticism with surprising equanimity.
examples.translation: Manejó las críticas con una serenidad sorprendente.

vocabulary.notes: A formal word often used for calm under pressure.

definition.en: To make something less harmful, severe or painful
definition.es: Hacer algo menos dañino, grave o doloroso

examples.sentence: A short walk can mitigate the effects of prolonged sitting.
examples.translation: Un paseo corto puede mitigar los efectos de estar sentado mucho tiempo.

vocabulary.notes: Usually takes an object: mitigate the risk, not mitigate against the risk.

definition.en: Bringing strong images, memories or feelings to mind
definition.es: Que evoca imágenes, recuerdos o sentimientos intensos

examples.sentence: The film's evocative score made the empty house feel inhabited.
examples.translation: La música evocadora de la película hizo que la casa vacía pareciera habitada.

vocabulary.notes: Common in criticism of art, writing, film and music.

definition.en: Concerned with beauty, appearance or artistic principles
definition.es: Relacionado con la belleza, la apariencia o principios artísticos

examples.sentence: The aesthetic restraint made the final image more powerful.
examples.translation: La contención estética hizo más potente la imagen final.

vocabulary.notes: In British English, aesthetic is pronounced with a long ee sound.

definition.en: To place two contrasting things close together for comparison
definition.es: Colocar dos cosas contrastantes juntas para compararlas

examples.sentence: The exhibition juxtaposed archival photographs with new portraits.
examples.translation: La exposición yuxtaponía fotografías de archivo con retratos nuevos.

vocabulary.notes: The verb is transitive: juxtapose A with B.

definition.en: Less important than the central part of something
definition.es: Menos importante que la parte central de algo

examples.sentence: The peripheral details quietly changed the meaning of the scene.
examples.translation: Los detalles periféricos cambiaron en silencio el sentido de la escena.

vocabulary.notes: It can also mean located at the edge of a physical area.

definition.en: Based on deep physical or emotional feelings rather than thought
definition.es: Basado en sentimientos físicos o emocionales profundos

examples.sentence: The memoir prompted a visceral response from its audience.
examples.translation: Las memorias provocaron una respuesta visceral del público.

vocabulary.notes: Often describes an intense reaction that is felt physically.

definition.en: Medically dangerous because it can spread and cause serious harm
definition.es: Maligno; peligroso porque puede extenderse y causar daño grave

examples.sentence: The scan revealed a small but malignant growth.
examples.translation: La exploración reveló un crecimiento pequeño pero maligno.

vocabulary.notes: In general English it can also mean deliberately harmful or spiteful.

definition.en: Relating to the chemical processes by which living cells produce energy
definition.es: Relacionado con los procesos químicos que producen energía en las células

examples.sentence: Sleep affects several metabolic processes.
examples.translation: El sueño afecta a varios procesos metabólicos.

vocabulary.notes: The noun is metabolism.

definition.en: A medical forecast of how a disease or condition will develop
definition.es: Pronóstico médico sobre cómo evolucionará una enfermedad

examples.sentence: Early treatment significantly improved the patient's prognosis.
examples.translation: El tratamiento temprano mejoró significativamente el pronóstico del paciente.

vocabulary.notes: It is a forecast, not a certainty.

definition.en: Very severe or sudden; in medicine, of rapid onset
definition.es: Muy intenso o repentino; en medicina, de aparición rápida

examples.sentence: The clinic was designed for acute cases requiring immediate care.
examples.translation: La clínica se diseñó para casos agudos que requieren atención inmediata.

vocabulary.notes: It can also mean perceptive, as in acute awareness.

definition.en: Not intentional; resulting from carelessness or inattention
definition.es: No intencionado; causado por descuido o falta de atención

examples.sentence: An inadvertent change in dosage caused the discrepancy.
examples.translation: Un cambio accidental en la dosis causó la discrepancia.

vocabulary.notes: A useful formal alternative to accidental.

definition.en: Having a useful or beneficial effect, especially by correcting behavior
definition.es: Que tiene un efecto beneficioso, especialmente al corregir una conducta

examples.sentence: The setback was a salutary reminder to check the data.
examples.translation: El revés fue un recordatorio beneficioso para revisar los datos.

vocabulary.notes: Often describes a difficult experience that teaches something valuable.

definition.en: Very easy to see or notice
definition.es: Muy fácil de ver o notar; llamativo

examples.sentence: The conspicuous absence of data weakened the report.
examples.translation: La ausencia llamativa de datos debilitó el informe.

vocabulary.notes: It can describe something visually obvious or socially remarkable.
